definitions.explanation: A house or building constructed with only one floor, no upper stories. Often used in real estate listings and discussions of housing preference.

examples.japanese: {平屋|ひらや}{建|だ}ての{家|いえ}に{住|す}んでいる。
examples.english: I live in a single-story house.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{平屋|ひらや}{建|だ}ての{家|いえ}を{建|た}てた。
examples.english: My grandfather built a single-story house.

examples.japanese: {年|とし}を{取|と}ったら{階段|かいだん}のない{平屋|ひらや}{建|だ}てに{住|す}みたいと{思|おも}っている。
examples.english: When I get older, I'd like to live in a single-story house with no stairs.

notes:
Compound of {平屋|ひらや} (single-story building) + {建|だ}て (constructed as). Often shortened to just {平屋|ひらや}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {平屋|ひらや}{建|だ}ての{家|いえ}: single-story house
- {平屋|ひらや}{建|だ}てを{建|た}てる: to build a single-story house
- {平屋|ひらや}{建|だ}てに{住|す}む: to live in a single-story house

CULTURAL NOTE:
Single-story homes are increasingly popular among older Japanese couples and retirees because they avoid stairs and are easier to maintain. They are also associated with rural and traditional housing.

RELATED WORDS:
- 〜{階|かい}{建|だ}て: ~storied (general counter pattern for number of floors)
- {二|に}{階|かい}{建|だ}て: two-story (the most common urban housing form)
